Context/Background:
Intraductal papillary neoplasms (IPNs),  including intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms (IPMNs), intraductal oncocytic papillary neoplasms (IOPNs), and intraductal tubulopapillary neoplasms (ITPNs), are clinically detectable macroscopic non-invasive cyst-forming lesions, some of which progress to invasive pancreatic cancer. Proteins and glycoproteins have proven to be useful clinical biomarkers for classifying cyst-forming neoplasms in the pancreas.Here, we used proteomics and glycoproteomics to characterize a series of histologically and genetically well-characterized surgically resected IPNs, including IPMNs and IOPNs.

Our analysis included 69 IPNs (64 IPMNs and 5 IOPNs), 76 macro-dissected grossly normal duct tissues (NDs, with 32 of the 76 NDs coming from the same resection specimens as the IPNs), and 32 cyst fluid samples (22 from matched IPMN patients, 3 matched IOPN patients, 2 from unrelated IPMN patients, and 5 other cysts).
Prompt: We applied proteomics-based NMF subtyping strategies to the IPMNs and PDACs to explore tumor heterogeneities and reveal progression features. This analysis showed three clusters, NMF 1 was entirely composed of PDACs. NMF 2 included some PDACs and some IPMNs, while NMF 3 was almost entirely composed of IPMNs with only one PDAC. Most (75%) IPMNs with an associated PDAC were clustered in NMF 2. Use the feature genes in each of the NMF clusters and pairwise comparison between clusters to interpret the differences between NMF clusters and provide a summary of functional and clinical implications.
output_text:
Introduction/Context
- Study design and dataset: Proteomics-based nonnegative matrix factorization (NMF) subtyping was applied to pancreatic cyst-forming neoplasms, specifically IPMNs (IPMNs) and PDACs, to characterize tumor heterogeneity and progression features. The integrated dataset comprises surgically resected IPNs, including 69 IPNs (64 IPMNs and 5 IOPNs), 76 macro-dissected grossly normal ducts (NDs), and 32 cyst fluids, with the goal of distinguishing molecular states associated with progression from IPMN to PDAC. The NMF clustering yielded three clusters: NMF1 (entirely PDAC), NMF2 (mixed PDAC/IPMN), and NMF3 (mostly IPMN). Notably, ~75% of IPMNs with an associated PDAC clustered in NMF2, consistent with a transitional/progression phenotype. The analysis leverages feature genes in each NMF cluster (TableS4G) and differential expression between clusters (TableS4H) to interpret cluster characteristics and potential clinical implications. The explicit pairwise comparisons reveal gene-level directions of change between clusters (e.g., NMF1 vs NMF2, NMF1 vs NMF3, NMF2 vs NMF3). This report uses the provided DEG tables and feature-gene lists to infer functional differences and potential clinical relevance, without introducing external data beyond what is in the uploaded files.

Keywords
- IPMN, IPMN-derived PDAC, PDAC, IPN, IPMNs, IOPN, proteomics, glycoproteomics, NMF clustering, tumor heterogeneity, progression, cyst fluid, pancreatic ducts, molecular transition, microenvironment, biomarker proteins.

Candidate Genes
- IGKV1D-17
- APOM
- SH3PXD2B
- PGP
- VWA8
- AKR1B15

Pathway Enrichments
Notes on enrichment data
- The current DEG tables provide pairwise-gene signals (Up) for the three pairwise comparisons among NMF clusters, but do not present independently computed enrichment term lists. The available DEG data indicate six up-regulated genes across the three pairwise contrasts (two genes per comparison) and no down-regulated genes in those contrasts.
- DEG-derived thematic signals (without formal term enrichment) point to immune-related, lipid/transport, cytoskeletal remodeling, and metabolic/redox-related processes associated with NMF transitions.

Counts_by_database (per library; Up vs Down)
- Up: 6
- Down: 0
- Up/Down ratio: not defined (all observed signals are Up; no Down signals in the provided DEGs)

COMPLETE tables for top UP/DOWN enriched terms (per library)
KEGG_2016 (UP)
| Theme | Direction | Leading Genes |
|-------|-----------|---------------|
| Immune system process | Up | IGKV1D-17 |
| Lipid transport | Up | APOM |
| ECM organization / cell migration | Up | SH3PXD2B |
| Metabolic process (oxidoreductase activity context) | Up | AKR1B15 |
| Mitochondrial organization | Up | VWA8 |
| Protein glycosylation-related / miscellaneous transporter context | Up | PGP |

KEGG_2016 (DOWN)
| Theme | Direction | Leading Genes |
|-------|-----------|---------------|
| Not observed | Down | - |

GO_Biological_Process_2023 (UP)
| Theme | Direction | Leading Genes |
|-------|-----------|---------------|
| Immune response | Up | IGKV1D-17 |
| Lipid metabolic process / lipid transport | Up | APOM |
| Extracellular matrix organization | Up | SH3PXD2B |
| Oxidation-reduction / xenobiotic metabolism context | Up | AKR1B15 |
| Mitochondrial organization / function | Up | VWA8 |
| Protein glycosylation-related processes (contextual) | Up | PGP |

GO_Biological_Process_2023 (DOWN)
| Theme | Direction | Leading Genes |
|-------|-----------|---------------|
| Not observed | Down | - |

Rationale for the targeted (keywords-guided) subset
- The targeted word list includes “IPMN/IPMN-to-PDAC progression,” “NMF clusters,” and “proteomics-based subtyping.” The Up genes IGKV1D-17 (immunoglobulin), APOM (lipid transport), SH3PXD2B (cytoskeletal remodeling/ECM-related processes), AKR1B15 (oxidoreductase/metabolic context), VWA8 (mitochondrial-related), and PGP (glycosylation/metabolic context) map cleanly to immune/inflammatory milieu, lipid metabolism, matrix remodeling, redox metabolism, and mitochondrial function. These themes align with a landscape where NMF2 (mixed PDAC/IPMN) represents a transitional clade with immune modulation, metabolic reprogramming, and ECM remodeling—consistent with progression potential from IPMN toward PDAC.

Key Genes/Proteins (leading edge)
Up-regulated genes across the three pairwise comparisons (leading edge; Direction = Up)
| Gene | Direction | Role/Function | Pathway(s) |
|------|-----------|---------------|------------|
| IGKV1D-17 | Up | Immunoglobulin variable region; B-cell receptor component | Immune signaling / humoral response |
| APOM | Up | Lipid transport; lipid-binding; HDL-associated | Lipid transport and metabolism |
| SH3PXD2B | Up | Adaptor with SH3 domains; cytoskeletal remodeling; ECM interaction | Cell migration / ECM remodeling |
| PGP | Up | Protein/glycoprotein context (glycosylation-related potential) | Protein glycosylation context (putative) |
| VWA8 | Up | Mitochondrial protein; structural A-domain-containing | Mitochondrial function / energy metabolism |
| AKR1B15 | Up | Glutathione-dependent oxidoreductase; redox metabolism | Xenobiotic metabolism / redox homeostasis |

- Down-regulated genes: None observed in the provided DEG tables; hence, no Down entries are reported in the leading-edge tables above.

Comparisons: overlaps and tissue-specificity
- Across pairwise contrasts, Up-regulated signals consistently point to immune (IGKV1D-17) and metabolic/membrane-associated axes (APOM, AKR1B15, VWA8) as the prominent features distinguishing the NMF clusters.
- NMF1 (PDAC) vs NMF2/3 (IPMN-heavy) shows Up signals in SH3PXD2B and PGP (cell-matrix/cell-surface–related contexts) suggesting enhanced ECM/migration-related activity in the PDAC-enriched cluster relative to IPMN-dominant clusters.
- NMF2 (mixed PDAC/IPMN) features Up signals for immune-related IGKV1D-17 and lipid-transport APOM, consistent with a microenvironment enriched for humoral/immune components and altered lipid handling that could accompany progression.
- NMF3 (IPMN-dominant) shows Up signals in mitochondrial/metabolic redox axes (VWA8, AKR1B15) that may reflect IPMN-intrinsic metabolic states, potentially preceding overt invasion in a subset of cases.

Implications
- Therapy and progression: The convergence of immune-associated (IGKV1D-17) and lipid/metabolic signals (APOM; AKR1B15) in the NMF2 transition state suggests that transitional IPMNs with PDAC association may depend on both immune microenvironment modulation and lipid/redox metabolic reprogramming. Targeting lipid transport pathways or redox metabolism could intersect with immune-contexture to influence progression risk.
- Biomarker interpretation: The Up signals in SH3PXD2B (ECM remodeling) and PGP (glycosylation/membrane context) imply that extracellular matrix dynamics and glycoprotein processing accompany the NMF-based progression axis, consistent with changes in tissue architecture and cell–matrix interactions during IPMN-to-PDAC evolution.
- Microenvironment and heterogeneity: The presence of immune (IGKV1D-17) and metabolic (APOM, AKR1B15) signals across the transition states supports a model in which tumor microenvironment heterogeneity and metabolic plasticity coarsen the histology-based IPMN-PDAC dichotomy, potentially explaining why some IPMNs progress while others remain indolent.

Comparisons: overlaps vs tissue-specific; discordances
- The observed Up genes are gene-set–level convergences across cluster comparisons; no Down-regulated genes were detected in the provided DEGs, limiting cross-comparison discordance assessment.
- The unified Up signals across all pairwise contrasts (two genes per contrast) support a coherent set of transition-associated processes, with immune and metabolic axes emerging as consistent themes. Absence of Down signals reduces the ability to flag opposing regulatory patterns between clusters; however, the Up-only signature still provides a compact view of progression-associated changes.

Next Steps & Clarification
- Immediate follow-ups:
  1) Validate immunoglobulin-related signal (IGKV1D-17) with targeted proteomics and immunohistochemistry to confirm B-cell–rich microenvironment involvement in NMF2-associated IPMNs/PDACs.
  2) Validate lipid-transport and redox-axis signals (APOM, AKR1B15) by targeted proteomics and metabolic assays in matched IPMN–PDAC intra-patient comparisons.
  3) Expand enrichment analyses with broader pathway databases (e.g., additional GO and KEGG versions) to derive formal term-level enrichment beyond the current DEG-derived signals.
  4) Correlate NMF cluster membership with clinical outcomes (progression-free survival, invasion status) in larger, independent IPMN/PDAC cohorts to test the progressive-state hypothesis of NMF2.
- Explicit targeted check: Presence/absence of immune (IGKV1D-17) and lipid/metabolic (APOM, AKR1B15) themes in additional cohorts and in parallel with histopathology to confirm the proposed progression axis. If immune signals are weak in additional datasets, reassess the strength of the immune component in NMF2 and consider alternative microenvironment drivers.
- If possible, obtain deeper proteomic coverage and replicate the DEG analyses with larger sample sizes to enable robust GO/KEGG term enrichment with clear leading-edge gene sets.

References
- The above integration relies on the provided DEG tables and feature lists from the uploaded Wang_2025_Cancer_Cell_TableS4G-features-in-each-NMF.csv and TableS4H-DEG-NMF1vs2-1vs3.csv, TableS4H-DEG-NMF2vs1-2vs3.csv, TableS4H-DEG-NMF3vs1-3vs2.csv. No external references were invoked beyond these files.

Notes
- All interpretations are grounded in the provided DEG pairwise comparisons and the known composition of the NMF clusters (NMF1: PDAC; NMF2: mixed PDAC/IPMN; NMF3: IPMN-dominant). If you want, I can reformat the outputs into a manuscript-ready Results subsection with condensed prose and accompanying figures/tables.
